questions.question: Directions: Each item in this section consists of sentences with an underlined word followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the answer sheet accordingly. The village fair was cancelled due to incessant rains.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Each item in this section consists of sentences with an underlined word followed by four words or group of words. Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response on the answer sheet accordingly.

The village fair was cancelled due to incessant rains.
questions.solution: The word "incessant" means never stopping (and usually annoying). Example: The region endured weeks of incessant rain. The antonym of "incessant" is "sporadic." The word "sporadic" means not done or happening regularly. Example: More than 100 people have been killed this year in sporadic outbursts of ethnic violence.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Memory
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Memory
questions.solution: The word "Memory" means a person’s ability to remember things. Example: After the accident he suffered from loss of memory. The antonym of "Memory" is "Oblivion." The word "Oblivion" means a state in which you do not realize what is happening around you, usually because you are unconscious or asleep. Example: I was in a state of complete oblivion.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. He was compelled by everyone to join the group.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

He was compelled by everyone to join the group.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Dissuaded."

Key Points 
  • Antonym means a word that has the opposite meaning of the given word.
  • Let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
    • "Compelled" means forced or pressured to do something.(मजबूर)
      • Example: Her family compelled her to take the job.
    • "Dissuaded" means being discouraged or advised against doing something.(रोक)
      • Example: He was finally dissuaded to ignore the matter.
  • Therefore, it can be concluded that the word "dissuaded" is the antonym of "compelled."

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Additional Information

  • Demur means to object or hesitate.(आपत्ति)
  • Obscured means to make unclear or difficult to understand.(अस्पष्ट करना)
  • Confessed means to admit or acknowledge a wrongdoing.(स्वीकार करना)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Do you know the old adage 'the show must go on’?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Do you know the old adage 'the show must go on’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Misconstruction."

Key Points 
  • The question asks for an antonym of the underlined word.
  • The underlined word is 'adage.'
  • "Adage" means a saying that sets forth a general truth and that has gained credit through long use (एक पुरानी और प्रसिद्ध कहावत जो एक आम सच्चाई को व्यक्त करती है।).
    • Example: He remembered the old adage, "Look before you leap."
  • The word "misconstruction" means a false interpretation of evidence , facts, etc.
    • Example: Any misconstruction of these terms could lead to errors of law.
  • Thus, it can be concluded that the word "misconstruction" is the antonym of the word "adage."

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.
Additional Information

  • Rebuke means to scold or criticize someone.
  • Dare means to challenge someone to do something risky or difficult.
  • Addiction means a strong dependence on a substance or activity.

Hinglish

  • Misconstruction: ग़लतफ़हमी
  • Rebuke: फटकार
  • Dare: हिम्मत
  • Addiction: लत

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Naïve’ from the given sentence. After years of working in politics, she had become naive and jaded, convinced that all politicians were cynical and that the system was rigged against the people.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Naïve’ from the given sentence.

After years of working in politics, she had become naive and jaded, convinced that all politicians were cynical and that the system was rigged against the people.
questions.solution: The word "Naive" means without enough experience of life and too ready to believe or trust other people. Example: I was too naive to realize what was happening. The antonym of "Naive" is "Cynical." The word "Cynical" means believing that people are motivated purely by self-interest; distrustful of human sincerity or integrity. Example: That was a cynical remark.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the opposite meaning of the underlined word. The explosive used is of my own formulation, and I can vouch for its efficiency.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the opposite meaning of the underlined word.
The explosive used is of my own formulation, and I can vouch for its efficiency.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Invalidate. "Vouch" means to confirm, attest, or guarantee the truth or quality of something. "Invalidate" means to disprove or make something null and void, which is the opposite. The meanings of the other words are: Maintain: To assert or keep up; Certify: To formally attest; Witness: To see or provide evidence for.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Risible
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Risible
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Serious. 

The meaning of "risible" is causing laughter or being laughable. 

The meaning of "serious" is solemn, not joking or not funny. 

The relation between them is that they are antonyms; "risible" pertains to something funny, while "serious" pertains to something not funny.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Mechanical
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Mechanical
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Manual.  
The meaning of the word "Mechanical" is operated by machinery or acting like a machine.  
The meaning of the word "Manual" is done by hand or operated by human effort.  
The relation between "Mechanical" and "Manual" is that they are opposites; "Mechanical" refers to machine operation, while "Manual" refers to human effort.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Meander
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Meander
questions.solution: The correct answer is: Direct. "Meander" means to follow a winding or indirect course, whereas "Direct" means proceeding in a straight line or without deviation. The meanings of the other words are: Ramble: To wander aimlessly (synonym); Depute: To delegate; Confirm: To verify.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. She has _____ (witty) remarks about everything.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.
She has _____ (witty) remarks about everything.
questions.solution: The correct answer is: unamusing. "Witty" refers to being clever and funny, whereas "unamusing" refers to being not funny or entertaining. The meanings of the other words are: Sorry: Feeling regret; Whimsical: Playfully quaint or fanciful; Woeful: Expressing sorrow or misery.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Catastrophe
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Catastrophe
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Success.

Key Points

  • The word "Catastrophe" means a sudden and widespread disaster or a momentous tragic event. (महाविपत्ति)
    • Example: The earthquake was a catastrophe that destroyed many homes and lives.
  • "Success" refers to the accomplishment of an aim or purpose, or the attainment of fame, wealth, or social status. (सफलता)
    • Example: After years of hard work, she finally achieved great success in her career.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Success.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Nurture (पालन ​​पोषण): To look after and protect somebody/something while he/she/it are growing and developing.
    • Example: The beauty of nature is unparalleled.
  • Immaculate (निर्मल ): Perfectly clean, neat, or tidy.
    • Example: She always kept her room in immaculate condition.
  • Disaster (आपदा): A sudden event, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe, that causes great damage or loss of life.
    • Example: The flood was a major disaster that affected the entire region.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Epitome
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Epitome
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Expansion.

Key Points

  • The word "epitome" means a perfect example of a particular quality or type. (सर्वोत्कृष्ट उदाहरण)
    • Example: She is the epitome of elegance and grace.
  • "Expansion" refers to the action of becoming larger or more extensive. (विस्तार)
    • Example: The rapid expansion of the company led to increased job opportunities.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'epitome' is 'expansion'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.
Note: Expansion has been marked as the correct answer in the official answer key.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Exhort (प्रोत्साहित करना): Strongly encourage or urge someone to do something.
    • Example: The coach exhorted the team to give their best performance.
  • Lucid (स्पष्ट): Expressed clearly; easy to understand.
    • Example: His explanation of the complex theory was remarkably lucid.
  • Precise (सटीक): Marked by exactness and accuracy of expression or detail.
    • Example: The instructions need to be precise so that there is no confusion.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. We should plan our actions judiciously before going to war.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
We should plan our actions judiciously before going to war.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Irrational.

Key Points

  • The word "judiciously" means using or showing good judgment, wise, or sensible. (विवेकपूर्ण तरीके से)
    • Example: We need to spend our money judiciously to make sure we don't run out before the end of the month.
  • "Irrational" refers to a lack of reason or logic; it means not based on reason or clear thinking. (अतार्किक)
    • Example: His fear of spiders is completely irrational.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of "judiciously" is "irrational".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Irrational.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Irreverent (असम्मानजनक): Showing a lack of respect for people or things that are generally taken seriously.
    • Example: His irreverent comments about the ceremony shocked everyone.
  • Irrelevant (अप्रासंगिक): Not connected with or relevant to something.
    • Example: The evidence presented in court was deemed irrelevant to the case.
  • Irritatingly (चिड़चिड़ेपन से): In a manner that causes irritation or annoyance.
    • Example: She tapped her pen irritatingly on the desk throughout the meeting.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Reluctant
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Reluctant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Enthusiastic.

Key Points

  • The word "Reluctant" means unwilling and hesitant; disinclined. (अनिच्छुक)
    • Example: She was reluctant to join the meeting because she was not prepared.
  • "Enthusiastic" refers to showing intense and eager enjoyment, interest, or approval. (उत्साही)
    • Example: He was enthusiastic about starting his new job next week.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Reluctant' is 'Enthusiastic'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Enthusiastic.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Desperate (बेकरार): Desperate means feeling a strong need or urgency, often because of hopelessness or distress.
    It expresses emotional intensity or anxious urgency, not willingness.
    • Example: She was desperate to find a job after months of unemployment.
  • Obedient (आज्ञाकारी): Obedient means following orders, not necessarily willingly. 
    • Example: The obedient dog followed all the commands of its owner.
  • Beautiful (सुंदर): Pleasing the senses or mind aesthetically.
    • Example: The beautiful sunset left everyone in awe.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Desolate
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Desolate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Festive.

Key Points

  • The word "Desolate" means a place that is empty and without people, making it appear sad and lonely. (उजाड़)
    • Example: The once bustling town is now desolate and abandoned.
  • "Festive" refers to something that is related to a celebration or festival, bringing joy and cheer. (उत्सव)
    • Example: The streets were decorated in a festive manner for the holiday season.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of "Desolate" is "Festive".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Festive.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Allusive (संकेतपूर्ण): Making indirect references.
    • Example: His speech was allusive, hinting at past events without directly mentioning them.
  • Frugal (मितव्ययी): Being economical with resources or money.
    • Example: She lived a frugal life, saving money wherever she could.
  • Melancholic (उदास): Feeling or expressing deep sadness.
    • Example: The melancholic music made everyone in the room feel somber.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The teammates made several jibes at the opponent team members during the interview.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
The teammates made several jibes at the opponent team members during the interview.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Consolation.

Key Points

  • The word "jibes" means mocking or taunting remarks. (मज़ाक उड़ाना)
    • Example: The kids exchanged jibes during the game.
  • "Consolation" refers to comfort received by a person after a loss or disappointment. (सांत्वना)
    • Example: She found consolation in the kind words of her friends after losing the match.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'jibes' is 'consolation'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Consolation.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Mockery (मज़ाक): Teasing and contemptuous language or behavior directed at a particular person or thing.
    • Example: His mockery of her accent was hurtful.
  • Inspiration (प्रेरणा): The process of being mentally stimulated to do or feel something, especially to do something creative.
    • Example: Her speech was a great source of inspiration to the students.
  • Contradict (विरोधाभास): Deny the truth of (a statement) by asserting the opposite.
    • Example: The witness's statements contradict each other.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Her behaviour was so ostentatious that it attracted the attention of everyone in the room.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
Her behaviour was so ostentatious that it attracted the attention of everyone in the room.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Restrained.

Key Points

  • The word "ostentatious" means characterized by vulgar or pretentious display; designed to impress or attract notice. (आडंबरपूर्ण)
    • Example: Her ostentatious outfit drew everyone's attention at the party.
  • "Restrained" refers to being characterized by reserve or moderation; unemotional or dispassionate. (संयमित)
    • Example: His restrained reaction to the news surprised everyone.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'ostentatious' is 'restrained'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Restrained.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Attractive (आकर्षक): Pleasing or appealing to the senses.
    • Example: She has a very attractive smile.
  • Gentle (सौम्य): Having or showing a mild, kind, or tender temperament or character.
    • Example: The gentle breeze was soothing on a hot day.
  • Repulsive (घृणित): Arousing intense distaste or disgust.
    • Example: The smell of the garbage was repulsive.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Foment
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Foment
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Regulate.

Key Points

  • The word "foment" means to instigate or stir up an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action. (उकसाना)
    • Example: He was accused of fomenting violence during the protests.
  • "Regulate" means to control or maintain the rate or speed of a machine or process so that it operates properly. (नियंत्रित करना)
    • Example: The government plans to regulate the financial market to prevent fraud.
  • Hence, the antonym of 'foment' is 'regulate'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Regulate.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Proximity (निकटता): Nearness in space, time, or relationship.
    • Example: The proximity of the school to my house is very convenient.
  • Remoteness (दूरस्थता): The state of being distant from something else, in particular from the main centers of population.
    • Example: The remoteness of the village makes it difficult to access healthcare.
  • Separation (विच्छेद): The action or state of moving or being moved apart.
    • Example: The separation of the two departments has led to better efficiency.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Intelligible
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Intelligible
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The word "Intelligible" means something that is clear and easy to understand. (सुबोध)
    • Example: His speech was intelligible to everyone present at the meeting.
  • "Incoherent" refers to something that is unclear, confusing, or not logically connected. (असंबद्ध)
    • Example: Her argument was incoherent and difficult to follow.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Intelligible' is 'Incoherent'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Sociable (मिलनसार): Willing to talk and engage in activities with other people; friendly.
    • Example: He is a sociable person who enjoys meeting new people.
  • Embezzle (गबन करना): To steal or misappropriate money placed in one's trust or belonging to the organization for which one works.
    • Example: The accountant was found guilty of embezzling company funds.
  • Deliberate (सोच समझकर किया हुआ): Done consciously and intentionally.
    • Example: It was a deliberate attempt to discredit the politician.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Forgive
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Forgive
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The word "forgive" means to stop feeling angry or resentful towards someone for an offense, flaw, or mistake. (क्षमा करना)
    • Example: She decided to forgive him for his past mistakes and move on.
  • "Loathe" refers to feeling intense dislike or disgust for someone or something. (घृणा करना)
    • Example: He loathes doing housework and always tries to avoid it.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'forgive' is 'loathe'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Unburden (भारमुक्त करना): To relieve someone of a burden or worry.
    • Example: She decided to unburden herself by sharing her problems with a friend.
  • Requite (बदला चुकाना): To make appropriate return for a favor, service, or wrongdoing.
    • Example: He sought to requite her kindness with a thoughtful gift.
  • Clear (स्पष्ट करना): To make free from confusion or ambiguity; to remove any doubts.
    • Example: The instructions were clear and easy to follow.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the opposite meaning of the underlined word. In front of the big screen, this behaviour is generally considered taboo .
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the opposite meaning of the underlined word.
In front of the big screen, this behaviour is generally considered taboo.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Acceptable.

Key Points

  • The word "taboo" means something that is socially or culturally prohibited or restricted. (वर्जित)
    • Example: Discussing personal salaries is considered taboo in many workplaces.
  • "Acceptable" refers to something that is deemed suitable, permissible, or satisfactory. (स्वीकार्य)
    • Example: Her proposal was found acceptable by the committee.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'taboo' is 'acceptable'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Acceptable.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Obedience (आज्ञाकारिता): Compliance with an order, request, or law or submission to another's authority.
    • Example: The dog's obedience to its owner was commendable.
  • Promotion (प्रचार): The action of supporting or actively encouraging a cause, venture, etc.
    • Example: The company is engaged in the promotion of its new product line.
  • Prescription (पर्चा): An instruction written by a medical practitioner that authorizes a patient to be provided a medicine or treatment.
    • Example: The doctor gave me a prescription for antibiotics.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Coy
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Coy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Extroverted.

Key Points

  • The word "coy" means being shy or modest, often in a playful or provocative way. (लजीला)
    • Example: She gave him a coy smile before looking away.
  • "Extroverted" refers to being outgoing, sociable, and openly expressive. (बहिर्मुखी)
    • Example: John is very extroverted and loves meeting new people.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'coy' is 'extroverted'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Extroverted.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Shy (शर्मीला): Being reserved or having a timid nature.
    • Example: He is too shy to speak in front of the class.
  • Upright (ईमानदार): Being honest or morally correct.
    • Example: She is known for her upright character and integrity.
  • Recent (हाल का): Something that happened a short time ago.
    • Example: The recent news of the merger surprised everyone.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Astute
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Astute
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Stupid.

Key Points

  • The word "Astute" means having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage. (चतुर)
    • Example: He was an astute businessman who could easily identify the best investment opportunities.
  • "Stupid" refers to lacking intelligence or common sense. (मूर्ख)
    • Example: It was stupid of him to forget the keys inside the car.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Astute' is 'Stupid'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Stupid.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Temporary (अस्थायी): Lasting for only a limited period of time.
    • Example: The temporary suspension of the service caused inconvenience to the users.
  • Illegal (अवैध): Contrary to or forbidden by law.
    • Example: Illegal activities such as smuggling are severely punishable.
  • Dispute (विवाद): A disagreement or argument.
    • Example: The land dispute between the neighbors has been going on for years.

questions.question: Select the correct antonym of the given word. Quiescent
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct antonym of the given word.
Quiescent
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. active

Quiescent: Refers to a period of inactivity or being dormant. (निष्क्रियता या निष्क्रिय होने की अवधि को संदर्भित करता है)

Active: Refers to someone who is willing to engage in physical pursuits. (किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति को संदर्भित करता है जो शारीरिक गतिविधियों में संलग्न होने को तैयार है)

For e.g. The health scare left Sania very active.

Thus, it is clear that quiescent and active are opposite words

Let's look at the meaning of other words:

  • Peaceful: Refers to something that is free from disturbance. (किसी ऐसी चीज को संदर्भित करता है जो अशांति से मुक्त हो)
  • Dejected: Refers to someone who is sad and depressed. (किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति को संदर्भित करता है जो उदास है)
  • Indifferent: Refers to someone who has no particular interest or concern. (किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति को संदर्भित करता है जिसकी कोई विशेष रुचि या चिंता नहीं है)

Thus, options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. VIGILANT
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.
VIGILANT
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. rash

Vigilant: Refers to someone who is very careful about possible dangers

Rash: Refers to someone who is careless and takes hasty decisions

Thus, it is clear that vigilant and rash are opposite words

Let's look at the meaning of the other words:

Wary: Refers to someone who is very careful and doubting

Alert: Refers to someone who is careful and aware

Sharp-eyed: Refers to someone who is very careful and observant

Thus, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sparse
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Sparse
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.

  • Sparse: thinly dispersed or scattered; scanty; in short supply
  • Abundant: existing or available in large quantities; plentiful
  • Tranquil: free from disturbance; calm
  • Costly: costing a lot; expensive
  • Scanty: small or insufficient in quantity or amount

Thus Abundant is antonym of sparse.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. HASTE
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

HASTE
questions.solution:
• Haste: excessive speed or urgency of movement or action; hurry.
  • Delay: make (someone or something) late or slow; a period of time by which something is late or postponed
  • Lose: be deprived of or cease to have or retain (something); become unable to find (something or someone)
  • Rush: move with urgent haste; dash towards (someone or something) in an attempt to attack or capture.
  • Dash: run or travel somewhere in a great hurry.

Thus, delay is the antonym of Haste.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Foul
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Foul
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
